idiom_name: func(T) error validator values + generic combinators; errors.Join for accumulation
implementation_notes: Go's function types are the carrier - type Validator[T any] func(T) error - and because Go has generics but no higher-kinded types the combinators are ordinary generic functions: an All/Any helper for divide and conquer, errors.Join to accumulate every failure instead of returning the first, and a closure over a projection for contramap. choose is a switch on a concrete interface value or a tag field, because Go sum types are hand-rolled. The standard library already consumes predicates in this shape (slices.ContainsFunc, IndexFunc, DeleteFunc), which is why predicates are idiomatic in Go while a typeclass hierarchy around them would be foreign; the struct-tag library (go-playground/validator) is the declarative realization for rules that belong to the data model.
pitfalls: Returning a typed nil from a func(T) error makes err != nil true on success (the interface holds a nil pointer); always return the untyped nil on the happy path.
errors.Join produces one multi-line message: if callers must match a specific failure, wrap each rule's error with %w so errors.Is keeps working.
A variadic generic combinator allocates the validator slice per call - build the composed validator once and reuse it instead of re-composing per item.
